adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:28 — Public `GET /groups/:group_id/members(.json)` response changed from a bare JSON array to `{members:[], meta:{}}` with no versioning, fallback, or deprecation window; every third-party consumer doing `result.map(...)` breaks at runtime

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (which yields a bare JSON array of users) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: ... }`, i.e., the top-level JSON shape is no longer an array. This is a backward-incompatible change to `GET /groups/:group_id/members(.json)` with no versioning or compatibility layer shown in the diff. Internal JS was updated (`Group.findMembers` now reads `result.members`/`result.meta`), but any external/third-party consumer expecting an array (e.g., doing `result.map(...)`) would break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — Default `limit 50` now applies to **all** groups (previously unlimited for non-automatic, 200 for automatic), but `templates/group/members.hbs` has no pagination UI — a 300-member public group silently renders only 50 with no error

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `GroupsController#members` the diff changes behavior to always apply pagination: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `members = ...limit(limit).offset(offset)` for *all* groups, whereas previously only automatic groups were limited/offset (default 200) and non-automatic groups returned the full list. On the client side, the public group members page (`discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6` + `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs`) now calls `model.findMembers()` and renders `{{#each m in members}}`, but the template adds no next/previous controls (pagination UI was only added to the admin group template). So a large public group will silently show only the first 50 members with no way to reach the rest via the UI in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:34 — `update_patch` was deleted but `resources :groups` still routes `PATCH /admin/groups/:id` → `update`; old incremental callers get HTTP 200 `success_json`, zero membership change, **and** the group silently flipped to `visible = false`

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `update_patch` and the `request.patch?` branching in `Admin::GroupsController#update`. Rails `resources :groups` will still route PATCH `/admin/groups/:id` to `update` by default, and the new `update` implementation ignores the old incremental `params[:changes]` payload (so no membership changes occur). Worse, it unconditionally does `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"`; if legacy PATCH callers omit `visible`, this sets `visible` to `false` and `group.save` likely succeeds, returning `success_json` (HTTP 200), causing a silent visibility flip.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:34 — `update` dropped the nested `group:` wrapper; an old-format caller sending `group[visible]=true` hits `params[:visible] == "true"` with nil → group silently made invisible, name/alias_level ignored, 200 returned

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Admin::GroupsController#update` to read `params[:alias_level]`, `params[:visible]`, and `params[:name]` directly, whereas the prior code read them from `params[:group]` (`payload = params[:group]`). With the new code, an old-format request that still sends `group[visible]=true` will have `params[:visible] == nil`, so `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` will set `visible` to `false` (and `alias_level`/`name` updates will be skipped because `params[:alias_level]`/`params[:name]` are absent). The action will still attempt `group.save` and can return success, making this a real backward-compatibility/correctness regression introduced by the diff unless all callers were updated in lockstep.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — `limit` is unbounded on a publicly reachable endpoint; `?limit=1000000` against `trust_level_0` dumps and serializes the entire user base — enumeration oracle plus memory/DB DoS. Widened by this PR, which now honors caller `limit` for every group

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff changes pagination to always do `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then `group.users.order(...).limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no upper bound or sanity check. That makes the publicly routed members endpoint honor arbitrarily large `?limit=` values and then serialize that many users, which can cause DB/memory/CPU pressure and enables bulk enumeration of large groups. This PR also widens the behavior from only `group.automatic?` (previously) to *all* groups, increasing exposure (even though automatic groups were already vulnerable to large limits).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:40,51 — `addMembers`/`removeMember` chain only success handlers; the callers at `admin-group.js.es6:56,64` discard the promise. A 422/400/404/validation failure produces no alert, no list change, no cleared input — indistinguishable from success

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Group#addMembers` and `#removeMember` do return the `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` promise and only reload the member list on success (no explicit `.catch`). However, the controller actions *do not* make success “indistinguishable” from failure: on success `findMembers()` reloads and the UI list will change; on failure the list will remain unchanged (member won’t disappear / new members won’t appear), which is observable. Also, the claim that a 4xx/5xx “produces no alert” is not verifiable from this diff because error handling may be provided globally by `Discourse.ajax`/app-wide AJAX error handlers. The only clearly verifiable part is the lack of local error handling and the TODO about clearing input, which is more of a UX improvement than a definite defect proven by the diff.

app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:20-38 — The load-bearing public change of this PR — new pagination and a new response envelope — ships with **zero** spec coverage; no `spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb` exists anywhere in the tree

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes `GroupsController#members` to add pagination params and return a new `{members, meta}` JSON envelope, and it does not add or modify any specs covering `GroupsController` in the shown changes (only `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb` is touched). adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:91-110 — Four incremental-membership specs deleted with no replacement, including "succeeds silently when adding non-existent users" and "succeeds silently when removing non-members" — precisely the edge cases the new code paths regress on (findings 12, 14)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the old “incremental” PATCH-based membership tests, but that behavior/API path was also removed (Admin::GroupsController#update_patch is deleted and membership changes moved to new add_members/remove_member endpoints). So the deleted specs no longer correspond to existing code, and their removal is not itself a verifiable defect. The claim that “the new code paths regress on” those edge cases is not supported by the diff: add_members still silently ignores non-existent usernames (it only adds when User.find_by_username succeeds), and remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id) which typically no-ops if the user isn’t a member. Therefore this finding is largely about test coverage and asserts a regression that isn’t demonstrated by the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:49-60 — `.update` retains one example with a negative assertion on an automatic group; the rewritten flat-param happy path (rename, `alias_level`, `visible`, error branch) is entirely untested — a regression where flat params are never read leaves the whole suite green

adjudication.rationale: The diff rewrites `Admin::GroupsController#update` to consume flat params (`params[:alias_level]`, `params[:visible]`, `params[:name]`) instead of the previous nested `params[:group]` payload, and also removes the prior spec coverage that exercised updating a normal (non-automatic) group and its attributes/members. The remaining `.update` spec shown only asserts that an automatic group ignores `name` changes and accepts `visible`, so there is no test proving the new flat-param happy path (e.g., updating `alias_level`, updating `name` for non-automatic groups, or failure handling) works. As a result, a regression in flat-param handling could slip by with the suite still passing, which is a verifiable test-coverage gap introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:65-97`, `config/routes.rb:48-50 — The only admin gate on `add_members`/`remove_member` is the routing-level `AdminConstraint`; the controller inherits staff-level `Admin::AdminController`. Controller specs bypass routing, so this privilege boundary has no test — moderator escalation would go unnoticed

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `add_members`/`remove_member` as actions on `Admin::GroupsController`, which inherits from `Admin::AdminController`. There is no evidence in the diff that these endpoints are only protected by routing constraints or that `Admin::AdminController` is “staff-level” (moderator-accessible) rather than admin-only. The new routes are also under the `/admin` namespace, so requests must match those constrained routes anyway. The claim about “moderator escalation” and “privilege boundary has no test because controller specs bypass routing” is speculative and not a verifiable defect introduced by this diff; it points to missing coverage of routing constraints rather than a demonstrable authorization bug in the changed code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — `group.users.delete(user_id)` passes a raw Integer; Rails resolves it via `find` on the association and raises `RecordNotFound` for a non-member, `user_id 0`, or a stale/duplicate click — the old `Group#remove` was an idempotent no-op

app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — `delete` on a `has_many :through` uses `:delete_all`: join rows go by raw SQL, skipping GroupUser callbacks and the `user_count` counter_cache. `groups.user_count` drifts upward permanently; both new specs assert `group.users.count` (live SQL) and never `group.user_count` — a textbook silent pass

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes member removal in `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member` to `group.users.delete(user_id)` (with a subsequent `group.save`). In Rails, `association.delete` on a `has_many :through` typically issues a direct DELETE on the join table (via `delete_all`) and does not instantiate/destroy the join model, so any join-model callbacks and counter-cache maintenance on `GroupUser` would be skipped. This is a plausible correctness regression compared to the previous pattern of `group.remove(user)` (used elsewhere in the diff in `add_members`), and the updated specs shown only assert `group.users.count` rather than `group.user_count`, so such drift would not be detected by these tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71-81 — `add_members` runs the `group.add` loop outside any transaction and before the `if group.save` gate; a mid-loop failure leaves earlier memberships committed while returning `render_json_error`. Unknown usernames are silently skipped yet still return `success_json`

adjudication.rationale: In `add_members`, unknown usernames are indeed skipped (`if user = User.find_by_username(username)`), but the diff provides no basis that this is a defect—earlier code/tests explicitly treated adding non-existent users as a silent success. The claim about partial commits from a mid-loop failure is not verifiable from the diff because it depends on how `group.add(user)` is implemented (not shown here) and whether it persists immediately or only mutates in-memory state until `group.save`. The method’s control flow (mutate then `group.save`) is normal and doesn’t by itself prove inconsistent persistence or incorrect success/error responses.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — N+1: one `find_by_username` per name plus one insert per user, with no cap on list size — a large paste means thousands of round-trips in one synchronous request. `User.where(username_lower: ...)` collapses it to two queries

adjudication.rationale: In the new `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames.split(",").each` and for each username performs `User.find_by_username(username)` and then `group.add(user)`. This is a classic per-item query pattern (one SELECT per username) and likely one INSERT per user added, all within a single synchronous request. There is no batching (`User.where(...)`) and no limit/guard on the number of pasted usernames, so a large input can trigger thousands of DB round-trips. This behavior is directly present in the diff and is a verifiable performance defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:22 — `create` never reads `params[:alias_level]` although the client's `asJSON` sends it; the admin's chosen alias level is silently discarded and the UI shows the stale selection until reload

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the client’s `Discourse.Group#asJSON` now sends `{ name, alias_level, visible }`, and `Group#create()` POSTs that payload directly to `/admin/groups`. However, `Admin::GroupsController#create` only sets `group.name` and `group.visible` and never assigns `group.alias_level` from `params[:alias_level]`. Therefore the chosen alias level is ignored on create and the persisted group will use the model default (likely 0). This is a concrete server-side correctness bug introduced by the changed request/params shape. (The UI may still show the selected value locally because the client doesn’t overwrite `alias_level` from the create response, but the saved value will be wrong until reload.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:23 — `offset`/`limit` have no lower bound; `?offset=-1` reaches Postgres as `OFFSET -1` and raises — an unhandled 500 from a publicly reachable endpoint. The JS clamp at `group.js:23` protects only the in-app caller

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. In `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members`, the diff sets `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then calls `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no clamp/validation. A request like `?offset=-1` will result in `offset(-1)` being sent to the DB (e.g., `OFFSET -1`), which PostgreSQL rejects (raises an exception), leading to an unhandled 500. The JS-side clamp added in `group.js#findMembers` only protects the Ember client and does not prevent direct requests to this server endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:25 — Newly added `total = group.users.count` runs a second full COUNT on every request, uncached, scaling with total membership rather than page size — and the page is refetched on every next/prev and after every add/remove. Derive from the existing `user_count` column

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members`, the diff adds `total = group.users.count` and then separately queries the paged members with `order(...).limit(limit).offset(offset)`. That introduces an extra COUNT(*) query on every members request (and the UI calls `findMembers()` on next/previous and after add/remove), so the DB work scales with total group size rather than just the current page. The codebase already tracks `user_count` on the Group model/serializer (used throughout the diff), so deriving `total` from that would avoid the extra full count query.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:20-48 — No in-flight guard or request sequencing; `findMembers` writes `offset`/`limit`/`user_count`/`members` from whatever response lands last. Rapid paging, or a removal overlapping a page change, leaves the page indicator and member list inconsistent

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js`, `findMembers` issues an async `Discourse.ajax(...)` and then unconditionally `setProperties({ user_count, limit, offset, members })` from the response. The controller/actions (`next`, `previous`, `removeMember` -> `findMembers`, `addMembers` -> `findMembers`, and route `setupController` calling `model.findMembers()` without awaiting) can trigger multiple `findMembers` calls while a prior one is still in flight. There is no cancellation, request token, or sequencing check, so an older/slower response can land after a newer one and overwrite `offset/limit/user_count/members`, making the paging UI (`currentPage/totalPages/showingFirst/showingLast`) inconsistent with the user’s most recent action. This is a real race introduced/present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:39 — After removing the only member on the last page, `findMembers` refetches with the pre-deletion `offset` clamped against a stale `user_count` — blank list at an offset past the new total, with no fall-back to the previous page

app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:33 — `next` clamps the new offset to `user_count` rather than the last page start `(totalPages-1)*limit`; a clamped offset is not a valid page boundary, so `currentPage` can disagree with the data shown
matched_golden_ids: In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same pagination bug: the `next` action clamps the offset to `user_count` (total) instead of the start offset of the last page, which can yield an invalid offset (e.g., offset == total) producing an empty/incorrect last page and inconsistent page display.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:21 — `findMembers` now returns bare `undefined` on the empty-name path where it previously returned `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])`, and on success resolves to `undefined` rather than the user array — a silent promise-contract break for plugins and for `next`/`previous`, which hand the value back to Ember
matched_golden_ids: Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that `findMembers` has execution paths that return `undefined` (missing/incorrect return), breaking the expected return/promise contract. This aligns with the golden issue of code paths without explicit returns yielding `undefined`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/routes/admin_group_route.js:11 — `setupController` never resets the singleton controller's `usernames`; text typed for group A persists onto group B and can add users to the wrong group — the same root cause as the author's own TODO (finding 34)

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the diff, `admin-group` controller changes `usernames` from a computed property derived from `members` (which would naturally be recomputed/overwritten when switching to a different group’s members) to a plain mutable property (`usernames: null`). Ember controllers are singletons reused across route transitions, and `AdminGroupRoute#setupController` now only sets `model` and calls `model.findMembers()`; it does not clear/reset `controller.usernames`. Since the template binds `{{user-selector usernames=usernames ...}}` and `addMembers` uses `this.get("usernames")`, whatever was typed for group A can remain when navigating to group B and be submitted against group B’s model, matching the described defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:10-12 — Split-brain state: the cursor (`limit`/`offset`/`user_count`) lives on the shared `Group` model while all paging logic lives on the admin controller, which mutates model state directly. The admin route reuses the instance from the `adminGroups` list, so `offset` survives leaving and re-entering the screen

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that pagination state (`limit`, `offset`, `user_count`) is stored on `Discourse.Group` and that the admin controller’s `next`/`previous` actions mutate `model.offset` directly before calling `findMembers()`. However, the key claim in the finding—“the admin route reuses the instance from the `adminGroups` list, so `offset` survives leaving and re-entering the screen”—is not verifiable from this diff. `admin_group_route.js` still resolves the model via `Discourse.Group.find(params.name)` and nothing in the shown changes proves that this returns the same object instance as the `adminGroups` list or that the object is reused across route transitions. Without evidence of caching/reuse semantics, the persistence behavior is speculative rather than a concrete defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6:8-12 — The public members route and the admin route drive the same Group model, but only the admin side has paging controls — the public list is capped at whatever cursor the shared model happens to hold, with no way to advance

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always return a paginated response (default `limit` 50, with `offset`) and changes `Discourse.Group#findMembers` to request `/groups/:name/members.json` with `limit`/`offset`, then store the results in `model.members`. The public route `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6` now just does `model.findMembers()` and the public template `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` iterates `{{#each m in members}}` with no next/previous controls (unlike the admin template/controller which adds paging actions). So the public members list will only show the first page (typically 50) with no UI to advance, which is a concrete behavioral regression introduced by this diff. The “shared model happens to hold a cursor” part is less certain (instance sharing), but the “capped with no way to advance” issue is verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs:1 — `{{#if model}}` used to guard the members array; `model` is now the always-truthy Group object. Dead guard reading as a loading/empty check that can never be false — the empty state is silently unhandled

adjudication.rationale: In `group-members` route, `setupController` now sets `model` to the Group object (`controller.set("model", model);`) and calls `model.findMembers()` to populate `members` asynchronously. In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs`, the diff shows it previously iterated `{{#each m in model}}` (so `model` was the members array), but now iterates `{{#each m in members}}`. Since the hunk starts at line 3 (`@@ -3,7 +3,7 @@`), any existing `{{#if model}}` guard at line 1 remains unchanged. That guard would now be checking the always-truthy Group object rather than the members array/loading state, making the conditional ineffective for empty/loading handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:22 — `create` dropped `usernames` support entirely with no migration path; callers must now do create + a second `PUT .../members`, non-atomic and undocumented

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `usernames` handling from `Admin::GroupsController#create` (old code set `group.usernames = ...` from `params[:group][:usernames]`; new code only sets `name` and `visible`). Correspondingly, the JS model/controller no longer sends usernames on create/save and instead introduces separate membership mutation endpoints (`PUT /admin/groups/:group_id/members.json` via `add_members`). As a result, creating a group with initial members now requires two separate requests (create, then add members), which is a behavioral/API change and is non-atomic (group can be created even if adding members later fails).

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:115 — `xhr :put, :remove_member` is asserted against an action routed only as `DELETE` (`config/routes.rb:49`); `ActionController::TestCase` ignores the verb, so the test exercises a request that cannot occur in production. Proof the suite has no routing-layer coverage
matched_golden_ids: The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same mismatch: the controller spec uses `xhr :put` for `remove_member`, but the route maps `remove_member` via a DELETE-only route (`delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member'`). The candidate adds extra context about the test not reflecting production, but the core issue matches exactly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:93-96,114-117 — The automatic-group 422 examples assert status only, never that membership was left unchanged; moving the guard below `group.add`/`users.delete` would land the mutation with both specs still green

adjudication.rationale: In the updated specs, the new automatic-group guard test for add_members only asserts the HTTP status (422) and does not assert that the group’s membership stayed unchanged. That’s verifiable in the diff under `context ".add_members"` (`"cannot add members to automatic groups"`), and it means a regression where `group.add(...)` happens before returning `can_not_modify_automatic` could still leave the spec green. The production controller currently guards before mutation, so it’s not a runtime bug, but the test coverage gap the finding describes is real in the diff (the remove_member portion is truncated, but the add_members case is clearly present).

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:52,55,94,115 — Specs hardcode seed `id: 1` / `group_id: 1` and assert negatively (`name.should_not == "WAT"`). Group 1 is already visible and already not named "WAT", so the assertions cannot distinguish "the guard worked" from "the action did nothing". `Fabricate(:group, automatic: true)` — already used at line 65 — makes this hermetic

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new specs that hardcode `id: 1` / `group_id: 1` (e.g., `.update` and `.add_members` contexts). These tests assume a particular seeded group exists with ID 1 and that it’s automatic, which is not guaranteed/isolated by the spec itself, making the tests non-hermetic and potentially brittle. Additionally, the `.update` spec asserts `group.name.should_not == "WAT"` and `group.visible.should == true`; if the seeded group already isn’t named "WAT" and is already `visible == true`, the test can pass even if the controller action failed to apply the intended guard logic (or even did nothing). Using a fabricated automatic group (as already done elsewhere in the file) would make the test verifiable and self-contained.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:62 — `params.require(:usernames)` then `.split(",")` assumes a String; `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b` yields an Array → `NoMethodError` → 500. Admin-gated, so impact is an unhandled exception

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the diff sets `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then immediately calls `usernames.split(",")`. In Rails, if a client sends `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b`, `params[:usernames]` will be an Array, and `Array#split` does not exist, causing a `NoMethodError` (500) because the code does not normalize/validate the type. The current JS client sends a comma-delimited string, but the controller code as written will crash for the array-shaped parameter.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:66,85 — `params.require` raises `ParameterMissing` → 400 with a non-JSON body, before any group/automatic check. The client has no handler on these paths, and where an error body *is* parsed (`admin-group.js.es6:85`, `$.parseJSON`), a non-JSON body makes the rejection handler itself throw

app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:62 — `// TODO: should clear the input` shipped in the action body; the user-selector keeps typed usernames after a successful add, making double-submits easy. Known-incomplete work committed as a comment rather than an issue

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the new `addMembers` action contains `// TODO: should clear the input` and then calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));` without ever resetting `this.usernames` (e.g., `this.set("usernames", null/"")`) either immediately or after the AJAX promise resolves. Since the template binds `{{user-selector usernames=usernames ...}}`, the entered usernames will remain in the input even after a successful add, making accidental repeated submissions plausible. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:46 — `removeMember`/`addMembers` call `self.findMembers()` inside `then` without returning it — the outer promise resolves before the list refreshes, and refresh failures are swallowed
matched_golden_ids: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same underlying problem: `findMembers()` is asynchronous but its promise isn’t properly handled/returned, so calling code may proceed before member data is refreshed/available, leading to a race condition (and potentially swallowed errors).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:47,58 — Each individual removal refetches the whole page including the unbounded COUNT (finding 19); trimming N members costs N page fetches + N counts instead of one

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js`, both `removeMember` and `addMembers` call `self.findMembers()` after the PUT/DELETE completes. `findMembers()` always issues an AJAX request to `/groups/:name/members.json`, and the new server implementation in `GroupsController#members` computes `total = group.users.count` on every request. Therefore, removing N members one-by-one triggers N extra member-list reloads and N full `COUNT(*)` queries (plus the DELETEs), which is a verifiable performance inefficiency introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:82 — `destroy()` returns `undefined` for an id-less group while `admin-group.js.es6:100` unconditionally calls `.then(...)`; deleting an unsaved group throws inside the bootbox callback, no error surfaces, and `disableSave` is never reset — Save stays disabled until reload

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `Discourse.Group.destroy()` returning `undefined` when `id` is missing (`if (!this.get('id')) { return };`), but that behavior already existed before this change (`if(!this.get('id')) return;`). The proposed finding’s key claim—that `admin-group.js.es6` “unconditionally calls `.then(...)`” on the result of `destroy()` and leaves `disableSave` stuck—cannot be verified from the provided diff because the `destroy` action/callsite in `admin-group.js.es6` is not shown/changed here. Since the problematic `.then(...)` usage and `disableSave` reset logic are not present in the diff, this is not a verifiable defect introduced or evidenced by the changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:34-47 — `.create` covers only name-stripping; the flat `visible` param, the `render_json_error` branch, and the `basic_group` response root the JS reads (`resp.basic_group.id`) are all unasserted — a serializer root-key change would break the admin UI with every Ruby spec green

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly notes that the updated `.create` spec only asserts name-stripping and does not cover other behaviors (flat `visible` param handling, error branch, or response shape). However, this is a test coverage concern, not a verifiable defect introduced by the diff: the client’s `group.create()` expects `resp.basic_group.id`, and `Admin::GroupsController#create` uses `render_serialized(group, BasicGroupSerializer)`, which is consistent with returning a `basic_group` root for a single serialized object in Discourse. There’s no concrete mismatch or failing behavior shown in the diff—only an untested contract that could regress in the future.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:80-89 — `refresh_automatic_groups` is pure mock verification (`Group.expects(...)` then assert 200) — asserts only that the controller calls the method it obviously calls. Pre-existing, not introduced here

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the `refresh_automatic_groups` spec still does `Group.expects(:refresh_automatic_groups!).returns(true)` then `xhr :post, :refresh_automatic_groups` and asserts `200`. That’s a weak/over-mocked test (it verifies the controller calls a method), but it’s not a functional bug/security/correctness defect in the application code introduced by the diff. It’s a test-quality critique, and the pattern also existed previously (it was just reorganized into a context).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/routes/admin_group_route.js:11-14 — The `setupController` fetch pattern is duplicated verbatim in `group-members.js.es6:8-12`; centralizing on a model hook or `loadMembers` would remove the copy and restore a lifecycle hook for loading/error state

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce very similar `setupController` logic in both `admin_group_route.js` and `group-members.js.es6` (setting the model and calling `model.findMembers()`), so the duplication exists. However, this is a DRY/refactoring suggestion rather than a clear defect: it does not demonstrate a bug, security issue, or correctness problem introduced by the change, and the claim about restoring lifecycle/loading/error handling is speculative and not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/admin/admin_base.scss:164 — `.form-horizontal` rules lifted out of `section.details` and re-parented under a shared `.groups, .badges` selector — not pure formatting; the badges form's rules now apply at a different scope and specificity, coupling two unrelated admin areas

adjudication.rationale: The diff does re-parent common `.form-horizontal` styling from `section.details .form-horizontal` into a new shared `.groups, .badges { .form-horizontal { ... } }` block and removes those rules from `section.details`. That change is verifiable. However, the proposed finding characterizes this as a defect (“coupling two unrelated admin areas”) without showing any incorrect behavior or breakage in the diff. Sharing base form styling between `.groups` and `.badges` is an intentional CSS organization choice, and the diff alone doesn’t demonstrate that badges now renders incorrectly or that specificity/scope causes a functional bug.
